sales_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to send an invoice by looking up or creating the customer record in {{vendor}}, our payments provider. If you don't already know the customer's details, ask me for: the customer's full name or company name, their email address, and (optionally) their billing address or any known {{vendor}} customer ID.

Actions to take:
1. Using the {{vendor}} API with our configured credentials, search for an existing customer matching the provided name and/or email address.
2. If a matching customer is found, confirm the match by showing me the customer's name, email, and {{vendor}} customer ID, and note any discrepancies (e.g., mismatched email or missing address).
3. If no matching customer is found, create a new customer record in {{vendor}} using the details I provided (name, email, and address if given).
4. After creating or confirming the customer, report back the final customer ID, name, and email so it can be used in the next step (generating the invoice).

Done looks like: you have either confirmed an existing {{vendor}} customer record or successfully created a new one, and you can clearly report the customer's {{vendor}} ID along with the name and email on file. If the search returns multiple possible matches, list them with enough detail (name, email) for me to pick the correct one rather than guessing.

Do not attempt to send the invoice yet — this step is only about resolving the customer record. Do not fabricate any customer details; if required information is missing, pause and ask me for it. Report your findings and the final customer ID back to me in a short summary.

sales_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me create a draft invoice with line items in {{vendor}}, our payments/invoicing provider, for a customer we've completed services for. This requires my explicit approval before anything is finalized or sent.

Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have:
1. Customer name/email (or existing customer ID in {{vendor}})
2. Line items: description, quantity, unit price, and currency for each service rendered
3. Due date or payment terms
4. Any notes or memo to include on the invoice

Actions to take:
- Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s API (or agent toolkit if available) to create a new draft invoice for the specified customer.
- Add each line item to the invoice with the correct description, quantity, and price.
- Set the due date and any notes as provided.
- Leave the invoice in draft/unsent status — do not finalize or send it.
- Prepare a summary showing: customer, all line items with totals, currency, due date, and the invoice's grand total.

What done looks like: a draft invoice exists in {{vendor}} with all line items correctly added, and you have a clear summary ready for my review.

Reporting back: Show me the full draft invoice details (line items, amounts, total, due date, customer) exactly as they will appear, along with a link or ID to the draft in {{vendor}} if available. Then stop for human sign-off — do not finalize, send, or charge the customer until I explicitly approve.

sales_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me send an invoice to a customer for services rendered using {{vendor}}, our configured payments/invoicing provider. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the customer's name and email, (2) a description of the services rendered, (3) the amount and currency, (4) due date, and (5) confirmation that {{vendor}} is already connected with my configured credentials.

Once you have these details, use {{vendor}}'s documented invoicing API or agent tool (for example, a send_invoice action) to draft a hosted invoice that includes the line items, amount, due date, and an online payment link, with automatic reminders enabled if {{vendor}} supports that feature. Prepare the invoice as a draft only — do not finalize, send, or trigger any charge or notification to the customer.

Once the draft is ready, summarize it clearly for me: customer details, line items, total amount, due date, payment link status, and reminder settings. Show me the exact draft content and any relevant confirmation screen or API response so I can review it.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, do not click send, confirm, or submit the invoice yourself. Present the completed draft and a short checklist confirming all details are correct, then stop for human sign-off. I will review and give final approval before the invoice is actually sent to the customer.

Report back with: the draft invoice summary, the tool or API call used to create it, any warnings or missing fields, and a clear statement that it is awaiting my approval to send.

sales_002:n4.prompt:
You are helping me track the payment status of an invoice I previously sent to a customer using {{vendor}}, our payments/invoicing platform. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (a) the customer name or invoice ID/number to look up, and (b) confirmation that you're authorized to use my configured {{vendor}} credentials to query invoice data.
2. Using my configured {{vendor}} credentials, look up the invoice and retrieve its current status (e.g., draft, sent, viewed, paid, partially paid, overdue, failed, or void). If {{vendor}} exposes a read/get-invoice style API or MCP tool, use it to pull the live status and any associated payment attempt details.
3. If the invoice shows a failed or unpaid status past its due date, check for any related payment failure or webhook event details available in {{vendor}} (e.g., decline reason, retry schedule) so I have context for follow-up.
4. Summarize what you find in plain language: invoice ID, customer, amount, current status, due date, and (if applicable) failure reason or last payment attempt date.
5. If the status indicates action is needed (e.g., payment failed, invoice overdue), draft a short, polite follow-up message to the customer requesting payment or offering to retry, but do not send it — prepare it as a draft for my review.
6. Do not send any customer communication, initiate retries, or take payment actions on my behalf — stop for human sign-off before any outbound message or retry action is executed.

Report back with: the invoice's current payment status, key details (amount, due date, customer), any failure/retry context found, and the drafted follow-up message (if one was warranted) for me to review and approve.
